subject: Private VPC networking follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex \u0014 thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on your Private VPC requirements.

Summary from our discussion:
- Deployment mode: Private VPC (you indicated preference for a non-public-hosted endpoint)
- Preferred connectivity: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) looked preferable from a security perspective; you mentioned VPC peering as a possible fallback.
- Region: likely us-west-2 (please confirm)
- Network: you said NetOps owns the CIDR choice; we discussed an allowlist approach for outbound traffic from your VPC to Redwood endpoints.
- Security: need mTLS/KMS integration, SOC 2 evidence, and audit logs.

Open questions for your NetOps team (please feel free to forward to whoever runs networking):
1) Confirm target VPC CIDR(s) and whether there are overlapping ranges with our service endpoints.
2) Do you prefer PrivateLink (interface endpoint -> our endpoint service) or VPC peering? Any org policy blocking interface endpoints?
3) Will you manage route tables for interface endpoints or want Redwood to provide step-by-step Terraform snippets?
4) Any strict egress allowlist requirements (specific IP ranges) or do you want to allow the Redwood endpoint DNS/resolved IPs?
5) Required certificates / mTLS process, and KMS key manager preference (AWS KMS / HSM).

Next steps I propose:
- Please share a short network diagram (CIDRs, VPCs) and NetOps contact.
- I'll attach our networking worksheet for your team to fill (see attachments).
- Schedule a 45-min NetOps deep-dive this week to walk through PrivateLink setup and required IAM roles.

Attachments: networking-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet to capture CIDRs/peering details)

If this looks right I can loop in Dylan (pre-sales infra) to outline the port/IP requirements and provide a Terraform snippet for PrivateLink.

Thanks \u2014
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0137

From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reid <tom.reid@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa \u2014 appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from our side and a couple of follow-ups from NetOps (cc'd Tom).

Answers:
- Region: confirmed us-west-2.
- CIDR: primary VPC is 10.20.0.0/16; we also have a management VPC at 10.50.0.0/16 (no overlap with your sample ranges).
- Connectivity: we prefer PrivateLink (interface endpoints) over VPC peering for security and least blast radius.
- Allowlist: we prefer explicit IP allowlists for outbound traffic and also terminating mTLS at the Redwood endpoint.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS; if Redwood supports customer-managed keys that would be ideal.

NetOps notes (Tom):
> We need to understand which ports and IPs will be used by Redwood endpoints. Also need an acceptance flow for VPC endpoint services (service name) and guidance on SG rules. We will not accept peering unless there are compelling reasons.

Attached is a quick network diagram and a primary NetOps contact (tom.reid@fintechcorp.com). Can Dylan join the NetOps call? Also we need any compliance checklist (SOC2 scope) included in the call.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Platform Engineering | FintechCorp
alex.jenkins@fintechcorp.com | (212) 555-0899

Attachment: fintechcorp-initial-network-diagram.png

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up and next steps

Alex / Tom \u2014 great, thanks for the quick answers and the diagram. Looping Dylan in as discussed.

What I'll do now:
- Attach our Private VPC networking requirements doc (redwood-private-vpc-reqs.pdf) and the networking worksheet for NetOps to populate. The doc includes the typical port list, endpoint service name pattern, and required acceptance steps for PrivateLink.
- Proposed Port/Protocol: TCP 443 (TLS) for inference API; additional ports 10250-10252 only if you intend to support diagnostic callbacks (most customers don't). We'll list minimal SG rules in the doc.
- KMS: we support integrating with customer AWS KMS; Dylan can confirm required IAM roles.
- Compliance: we will bring SOC 2 artifact access during the netops session and can share a redacted report under NDA.

Please pick a time for the NetOps deep-dive here: https://calendly.com/redwood-netops/45min. If you prefer, propose two time slots and we'll do our best to accommodate.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-reqs.pdf, networking-worksheet.xlsx

Thanks \u2014
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@fintechcorp.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up and next steps

Marissa / Alex / Tom \u2014 quick technical notes from pre-sales to prepare the NetOps call. Quoting Alex below for context:

On Thu, Jun 4, 2026 at 09:22 AM Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@fintechcorp.com> wrote:
> We prefer PrivateLink (interface endpoints) over VPC peering for security and least blast radius.
> CIDR: primary VPC is 10.20.0.0/16; management at 10.50.0.0/16

Technical summary / recommendations:
- PrivateLink (recommended): we'll publish an AWS VPC Endpoint Service in us-west-2. Your NetOps will create an interface endpoint that connects to this service (we will provide the service name). You will need to accept the endpoint connection in the console or via API.
- Security groups: allow outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from your workload SGs to the interface endpoint ENIs. We can provide a minimal SG rule: outbound 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443 from app subnets to endpoint (or narrow to endpoint ENI IPs if you prefer explicit IP allowlist).
- IP allowlist: If you require fixed IPs, we can provide a small set of stable egress IPs from our infra or recommend using the interface endpoint's ENI IPs. If using DNS-resolved addresses, please ensure DNS resolution in your VPC reaches the AWS resolver.
- mTLS / KMS: we support customer-managed AWS KMS for key wrapping and can support mTLS for mutual authentication. For mTLS we will need to exchange certs; otherwise standard TLS with client certs is doable.
- Terraform snippets: we'll share a sample TF module (private-link module) prior to the call. See link: https://drive.google.com/redwood-private-link-tf (will share access).

Suggested next steps:
1) Alex/Tom: confirm two available 45-min slots for NetOps deep-dive.
2) Tom: if possible, populate the attached worksheet with VPC IDs, subnets, and SGs.
3) Redwood: we will bring SOC2 scope and sample endpoint service name and TF snippet to the call.

Let me know if you want us to open a temporary demo endpoint for testing once connectivity is configured \u0014 we can spin up a dedicated PrivateLink service in your account for validation.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
